lineage.code_and_data_base: Historical v7.5.3 maintenance baseline, fully integrated into the v8.1 release
lineage.interface_contract: One Streamlit application provides eight visible sections, bundled or uploaded CSV analysis, reviewed RQ2-RQ4 result pages, examiner-facing literature traceability, and a separate optional Interactive Exploratory Sandbox.
lineage.integration_boundary: Reviewed Q3 and Q4 pages read the packaged experiment outputs without training. Only the optional Analyze Your Data page can fit an exploratory model after an explicit button click.

title: Design and Evaluation of a Reproducible Five-Session Machine-Learning Dashboard for Stock-Trend Classification and Downstream Decision Analysis
aim: To design and technically validate a reproducible local AI research dashboard that links a five-session stock-trend target, pre-specified feature-family evaluation, common-information model comparison, and cross-asset downstream decision analysis.

RQ1.text: Can the Capstone I proof of concept be delivered as a working local research Dashboard that visibly connects data preparation, feature evaluation, machine-learning comparison, cross-asset replication, and downstream analysis?
RQ1.scope: Successful implementation and display of the working eight-section Dashboard, with traceable reviewed results and a separate optional exploratory user-data workflow.

RQ2.text: Under an identical regularised Logistic Regression framework, how does retrospective walk-forward classification performance differ across four pre-specified standalone feature families—EMA-aware technical, cross-market, macroeconomic, and broad sentiment/risk proxies—when predicting Tesla's five-session forward-versus-trailing mean-close direction?
RQ2.scope: TSLA-only feature-family comparison under one common linear model; 1,250 Development OOF predictions and a 407-row retrospective audit.

RQ3.text: Using the pre-specified EMA-aware Technical feature specification identified in RQ2, how do regularised Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost and a compact LSTM compare in retrospective walk-forward prediction of Tesla's rolling five-session mean-price trend, and does any nonlinear or sequential model provide robust incremental predictive value over linear and transparent trend baselines?
RQ3.scope: TSLA common-information 20 by 6 model-family comparison, nested temporal evaluation, Development-only one-SE selection, and retrospective temporal audit.

RQ4.text: To what extent do the predictions generated by Lagged Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost and Compact LSTM translate into five-session downstream decision performance relative to Buy-and-Hold and transparent moving-average baselines, and how consistent are the observed outcomes across TSLA, AAPL and NVDA?
RQ4.scope: Descriptive five-session application-layer evaluation across three separately fitted assets; no RQ4 bootstrap, p-value, significance claim, return-driven model reselection, or rolling-retraining comparison.

O1.text: To implement and display a working local Streamlit Dashboard that connects the RQ1-RQ4 workflow and keeps reviewed results separate from optional exploratory training.

O2.text: To compare four standalone TSLA feature families using a common regularised Logistic Regression and five-session target.

O3.text: To compare four predictive model families under the pre-specified EMA-aware six-feature, 20-session information design and select conservatively using Development data only.

O4.text: To operationalise four reviewed model prediction streams through one five-session decision layer and describe their cross-asset return, drawdown, exposure, and temporal-stability patterns.

target.name: Rolling five-trading-session mean-price trend
target.interpretation_boundary: This is a five-session mean-price trend class, not a trading win rate or a fifth-session endpoint-return label.

rq3_information_design.common_information_rule: All four RQ3 models receive the same six feature streams over t-19 through t; tabular models receive the ordered 120-value flattening and Compact LSTM receives the 20 by 6 tensor.

decision_layer.signal: Probability >= 0.50 maps to long; otherwise cash.
decision_layer.target_alignment_boundary: The five-session decision horizon is aligned with RQ3, but Open[t+1] to Open[t+6] return is not mathematically identical to the future-mean-close target.

system_evidence.purpose: RQ1 completion through a working eight-section Dashboard with technical traceability.
system_evidence.evaluation: Local Streamlit execution, eight-section interaction, CSV upload, reviewed RQ2-RQ4 pages that do not train models, an optional button-triggered Interactive Exploratory Sandbox, and automated technical checks.
system_evidence.claim_boundary: RQ1 is answered by delivery and display of the working Dashboard; formal pages render reviewed saved results rather than retraining during presentation.

quantitative_feature_family_comparison.evaluation: Five retrospective Development walk-forward folds plus a later retrospective audit under the common five-session target.
quantitative_feature_family_comparison.claim_boundary: The comparison does not establish that one feature family is universally superior across models, assets, or future periods.

quantitative_model_comparison.evaluation: Nested retrospective temporal evaluation with a common 20 by 6 input, five Development outer folds, a fixed 0.50 threshold, Development-only one-SE selection, and a later retrospective audit.
quantitative_model_comparison.claim_boundary: Observed classification ranks and the one-SE selection do not prove unique model superiority or future stability.

descriptive_downstream_evaluation.purpose: RQ4 prediction-to-decision conversion and cross-asset replication.
descriptive_downstream_evaluation.evaluation: Five self-financing 20% sleeves, next-open execution, five-session holding, fixed 15 bps one-way friction, Buy-and-Hold, EMA8/13 and SMA10/20 references, exposure measures, and Development/later-period reporting.
descriptive_downstream_evaluation.claim_boundary: RQ4 is descriptive: it uses no RQ4 bootstrap, p-value, significance claim, quarterly rolling retraining, or return-driven tuning.

validation_summary.boundary: Saved analytical checks support reproducibility and internal consistency; they are not prospective validation.

claim_boundaries: All 2016-2026 evidence is retrospective; the later period is not a prospectively untouched holdout.
AAPL and NVDA are asset-specific pipeline replications, not zero-shot transfer of a TSLA-trained model.
RQ4 return results do not alter RQ2 feature choice, RQ3 model selection, thresholds, or hyperparameters.
RQ4 is descriptive and does not use a bootstrap, p-value, statistical-superiority claim, or rolling-retraining comparison.
Historical backtests under simplified fixed costs do not establish future or live profitability.
Interactive Sandbox outputs are exploratory and cannot replace the reviewed experiment results.
